{
  "summary": "Removes AssumeUTXO snapshot loading (loadtxoutset), background historical validation, and multi-chainstate infrastructure across the codebase. Collapses ChainstateManager, block downloading, cache allocation, pruning boundaries, and block storage cursors back down to a single active chainstate. Replaces dynamic coins database reopening with direct ownership by value, and rejects startup on datadirs with active snapshot markers while preserving dumptxoutset exports and standard assumevalid validation.",
  "problem": "Supporting concurrent chainstates requires pervasive special-casing across block download, cache management, LevelDB lifecycles, indexers, prune heights, wallet rescans, and validation interface notifications. This introduces significant architectural overhead and subtle synchronization complexity into core validation code for a feature that has seen low adoption.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description: 'Multiple chainstates affect much more than snapshot loading: ordinary validation changes have to account for different chainstate roles, candidate sets, notifications, downloads, pruning, cache allocation, database lifetimes and locks. I am not sure this amount of complexity in the most critical part of our codebase is still worth it, given that adoption isn\\'t where we hoped it would be.'",
    "PR description: 'Ordinary IBD is also getting faster: #35295 is already merged, and the upcoming pruneassumevalid will make pruned IBD even faster.'"
  ],
  "dependencies": {
    "depends_on": [],
    "enables": []
  },
  "scope_notes": "This is an explicit demonstration PR not intended to be merged directly ('not meant to be merged'), designed to serve as a reference for smaller, carved-out proposals. It removes over 5,000 lines of code across validation, net_processing, RPC, wallet, and storage components.",
  "changed_since_previous": "Rebased following the merge of test fixture refactoring in #36601 with minor diff adjustments, leaving the overall structure and scope unchanged.",
  "card": "This draft demonstration PR showcases the complete removal of AssumeUTXO snapshot loading, background synchronization, and multi-chainstate architecture across Bitcoin Core. It collapses ChainstateManager, block downloading, coins cache rebalancing, LevelDB lifecycles, and storage cursors back to a single active chainstate. The author states the PR is not intended for merge, but rather serves as a reference point for smaller proposals to simplify validation code. The change is motivated by low feature adoption, trust model ambiguities surrounding background validation, and the disproportionate complexity multiple chainstates impose on core validation, caching, and synchronization routines.",
  "needs": [

result.summary: Removes AssumeUTXO snapshot loading (loadtxoutset), background historical validation, and multi-chainstate infrastructure across the codebase. Collapses ChainstateManager, block downloading, cache allocation, pruning boundaries, and block storage cursors back down to a single active chainstate. Replaces dynamic coins database reopening with direct ownership by value, and rejects startup on datadirs with active snapshot markers while preserving dumptxoutset exports and standard assumevalid validation.
result.problem: Supporting concurrent chainstates requires pervasive special-casing across block download, cache management, LevelDB lifecycles, indexers, prune heights, wallet rescans, and validation interface notifications. This introduces significant architectural overhead and subtle synchronization complexity into core validation code for a feature that has seen low adoption.

I am not sure this amount of complexity in the most critical part of our codebase is still worth it, given that adoption isn\'t where we hoped it would be.'
PR description: 'Ordinary IBD is also getting faster: #35295 is already merged, and the upcoming pruneassumevalid will make pruned IBD even faster.'
result.scope_notes: This is an explicit demonstration PR not intended to be merged directly ('not meant to be merged'), designed to serve as a reference for smaller, carved-out proposals. It removes over 5,000 lines of code across validation, net_processing, RPC, wallet, and storage components.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased following the merge of test fixture refactoring in #36601 with minor diff adjustments, leaving the overall structure and scope unchanged.
result.card: This draft demonstration PR showcases the complete removal of AssumeUTXO snapshot loading, background synchronization, and multi-chainstate architecture across Bitcoin Core. It collapses ChainstateManager, block downloading, coins cache rebalancing, LevelDB lifecycles, and storage cursors back to a single active chainstate. The author states the PR is not intended for merge, but rather serves as a reference point for smaller proposals to simplify validation code. The change is motivated by low feature adoption, trust model ambiguities surrounding background validation, and the disproportionate complexity multiple chainstates impose on core validation, caching, and synchronization routines.

risk.why: Mistakes in consolidating chainstate initialization, coins cache ownership, or block download paths could lead to node crashes, chain synchronization failure, or database corruption.
